body.statement: There is a constant \(c_{\star}>0\) such that uniformly in the allowed designs and \(p,u\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\), \(\inf_{b,b'\in\mathbb R}\|a\mathbf 1+bq_N(p)-b'q_N(u)\|\ge c_{\star}|a|\) for every \(a\in\mathbb R\). The same bound holds on the diagonal \(u=p\) with the secant replaced by \(q_N'(p)\). For the ideal geometric curve \(q_N(p)=(1,t,t^2)^{\mathsf T}\), \(t=2^{2p-1}\), the normal vector \((tu,-t-u,1)^{\mathsf T}\) gives \((t-1)(u-1)\) against \(\mathbf 1\).
body.justification: Uniform secant and tangent separation identifies the slope even when the tail amplitude is zero and \(p\) disappears.
body.gap: Neither spectral-adjustment identification nor scalar quadratic variation contains this three-scale divided-difference modulus on perturbed designs.
body.consumer: It turns moment-space Gaussian radius bounds into root-\(N\) confidence-set diameter and risk bounds.
